newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland clears Ameritech sale of Centertel stake.
newsitem.headline: Poland clears Ameritech sale of Centertel stake.

text.p: Poland's anti-monopoly watchdog, the Office for Competition and Consumer Protection, said on Thursday it had cleared the planned sale by Ameritech Corp of its stake in the Centertel SA mobile phone operator.

The office's spokeswoman Jolanta Micel-Thor told Reuters Centertel's two other owners, France Telecom and Poland's state-owned telecom firm Telekomunikacja Polska SA could up their stakes above 33 and 51 percent respectively.
"The office has no reservations about France Telecom gaining more than 33 percent and TPSA more than 51 percent in Centertel," Micel-Thor said.

Telekomunikacja (TPSA) currently has 51 percent of Centertel with Ameritech and France Telecom holding 24.5 percent each. After sharing the Ameritech stake TPSA would have 64 percent and France Telecom 36 percent, newspapers said.

The partnership in the Centertel venture turned sour last year when TPSA, arguing its role in the company did not reflect its majority shareholding, began seeking more say in the firm's management and a bigger share in the company's profits.
Earlier this year TPSA blocked Ameritech and France Telecom's plans to seek one of two licences to develop a modern digital GSM system for Centertel, which now operates an older analogue system.
The licences went to two consortia of Polish and foreign companies, which have launched operations to challenge Centertel.

Ameritech and France Telecom have started international arbitration proceedings against Poland's government, saying that back in 1991 they were promised a GSM licence. The government argues the promise was not legally binding.
Newspapers have earlier quoted unnammed sources as saying Ameritech, which bought its Centertel shares for $36 million was now likely to sell it for $50 million.
